correctness.rationale: Exact tangent-chart differentiation of the specified normalized quadratic-eigenvector iteration yields independent two-state blocks \(P_j(z)=z^2-[1-\eta(1-p)\Delta_j]z+\eta p\Delta_j\). Three necessary-and-sufficient real-quadratic Schur inequalities collapse to restrictions at \(\Delta=L\), and standard discrete linearization proves local exponential attraction strictly within the interval. At and beyond its boundary the lowest-mode root reaches or exceeds the unit circle. Direct factorization of the critical Jordan matrix gives \(\|M^k\|_2=k+\sqrt{k^2+1}\). The standalone checker passed 288 spectral-root cases, 144 finite-difference actual-map derivative checks and 100 deterministic matrix-power/norm tests; these finite tests are supplemental, not exhaustive proofs.

originality.rationale: The 2026 original asynchronous Grassmannian source and closely related 2023 Riemannian aggregated PCA study provide sufficient convergence guarantees, not the specific exact necessary-and-sufficient mixture frontier or optimal stale proportion and critical Jordan power law. The scalar Schur/LMM test is explicitly recognized as prior mathematics; novelty is limited to the algorithm-specific full implication. Targeted mathematical-record searches found no coverage, subject to residual literature risk.
residual_risks: General multistep polynomial-stability theory is broad; a prior explicit specialization of the same two-step coefficients could subsume the scalar threshold, even though the eigensolver transfer was not located.
Selected pages rather than every page of the 2023 PDF were materially reviewed; an appendix could contain a closer special case.
No external independent novelty or correctness audit is available; literature search cannot certify global uniqueness.
The singular norm of a 2-by-2 shear is a standard calculation, not separately novel; value and originality concern the algorithm-specific joint phase boundary and its critical amplification.

value.rationale: A fixed one-iteration cache delay is a natural model in asynchronous principal-eigenvector extraction. The unique optimal 25% stale fraction doubles the sharp locally stable step ceiling from \(2/L\) to \(4/L\), while the exact linear Jordan growth at that ceiling gives a concrete safety obstruction. The result discriminates permissible local step size from faster convergence and is a motivated complete continuum-parameter classification, not an arbitrary sample value.
